findings.action:
Preserve Markdown block context before excluding code and comments. TrimSpace makes a four-space-indented literal fence delimiter into an opening fenced block: the valid Markdown body '    ~~~

Governs [the pair](../roadmaps/pair.md).
' loses its real association link. Separately, line 75 removes comments before recognizing code: '~~~
<!--
~~~

[real](../roadmaps/pair.md)

<!-- -->
' loses the real link because the literal comment opener inside code consumes through the later comment. Read-only reproductions of the production filter logic confirmed both losses. With two canonical members and no other association, closeoutADRAssociations reports no diagnostic and the evaluator grants Known=true, Required=false, contrary to R3. Respect indented-code and fenced-code context, including comment precedence, and add evaluator regressions in both association directions.

Parse balanced parentheses in inline Markdown destinations before resolving the association. The valid link '[decision](../adr/decision(extra).md)' to a regular canonical ADR file is matched as '../adr/decision(extra' by the production regex. The namespace filter then silently discards it because the truncated destination does not end in .md. I extracted and executed the exact production regex and confirmed that result. R3 permits basename .md ADR files without excluding parentheses and promises explicit local Markdown associations. A two-member roadmap whose sole association uses this link therefore receives an unjustified exemption. Parse the complete destination or return unknown for unsupported association syntax; cover forward and reverse links.
